Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node overweights the final-state relation and treats any positional change as progress. In the edited image, the original blue mug appears as a blurred remnant on the left, while two small mug-like objects are visible; the headphones are also altered. The trace does not establish which object is the original target or whether the requested mug was moved, and its claim that the mug is right of the headphones conflicts with the visible arrangement/identity ambiguity. Bind the target and reference to the same objects across source and edit, and require evidence of the requested target’s movement plus its final relation before calling completion. Distinguish established partial progress from unresolved identity or visual evidence; do not infer progress merely from a change or let supporting observations independently earn completion. The high-confidence ‘yes’ despite these ambiguities suggests the criterion/evidence aggregation needs calibration. No transport or schema failure is indicated.
s2: The node’s current “any relative-position change” criterion is too permissive: it can count an added or duplicated mug, an altered headphone, or an apparent change caused by image edits as progress without tracking the requested mug. Bind the mug and headphones across source and edit using visual identity and location/context, and assess whether that same mug has moved toward the requested right-of-headphones relation. Keep progress distinct from completion: this support check may establish a genuine movement even if the final relation is not achieved, but should not infer movement from a mug merely appearing on the right. In these images, the source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edit has a blurred blue remnant on the left and two small mug-like objects, with the headphones also changed. The trace does not resolve which mug, if any, is the original target, so this evidence warrants uncertainty rather than a high-confidence pass. Preserve an unknown outcome when identity or movement cannot be determined; do not treat the aggregate reference label as proof of this node’s atomic result. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
